intro.title: useTransition
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple search component that filters a list of names. You will learn how to use the React useTransition hook to manage state updates that should be treated as non-urgent, preventing the UI from freezing during slow updates. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the useTransition hook. You'll implement a loading indicator that shows during the transition, making your app feel more responsive. By the end, you'll understand how to mark certain updates as low-priority to improve user experience.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useTransition is essential for keeping the UI responsive during heavy state updates. You'll see this pattern in dashboard filters where selecting a date range triggers complex data fetching without freezing the interface. It's also used in e-commerce sites when applying multiple product filters simultaneously, allowing users to continue interacting with other UI elements. Form wizards that process data between steps benefit from useTransition to maintain smooth navigation transitions.
